request.title: Customer contact update API
request.description: Develop an API allowing customers to update their contact information. Validate mandatory fields, prevent unauthorized modification, maintain an audit record and return appropriate API error responses.

requirement_analysis.summary: Customer contact update API: expose an authenticated API that lets a customer replace their contact information (email, phone, postal address), validates mandatory fields, rejects modification by anyone other than the owner, writes an immutable audit record for every change and returns a consistent machine-readable error envelope.

functional_requirements.description: Expose an API endpoint that updates a customer's contact information (email, phone, address).
Validate mandatory fields (email, phone, address line 1, city, postal code, country) and their formats before persisting.
Authenticate the caller and only allow a customer to modify their own contact information.
Record an audit entry (actor, timestamp, request id, before/after state) for every successful update.
Return appropriate HTTP status codes (401, 403, 404, 422) with a uniform error envelope.

non_functional_requirements.description: Security: credentials and signing keys must come from configuration, not source; logs must not contain personal data.
Audit records are append-only and cannot be modified through the API.
Performance: p95 latency for the update endpoint under 300 ms at 100 req/s.
Logging/observability: every request carries a request id that is logged and stored with the audit entry.

business_rules.description: A customer may only update their own contact information.
Email, phone, address line 1, city, postal code and country are mandatory; the update is a full replacement.
Audit entries are immutable once written.

user_stories.goal: update my contact information through the API
user_stories.benefit: my records stay current without contacting support

user_stories.goal: have unauthenticated or non-owner update attempts rejected
user_stories.benefit: customer data cannot be tampered with

user_stories.goal: see who changed which contact fields and when
user_stories.benefit: regulatory audit requests can be answered
client applications can handle failures predictably

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated customer with a valid payload
acceptance_criteria.then: the API returns 200 with the updated record and the change is persisted

acceptance_criteria.given: a payload with a missing or malformed mandatory field
acceptance_criteria.then: the API returns 422 listing each invalid field and nothing is persisted

acceptance_criteria.given: a request without a valid bearer token
a valid token belonging to a different customer
acceptance_criteria.then: the API returns 403 FORBIDDEN and the target record is unchanged
exactly one entry exists with actor, request id, timestamp and before/after contact state

acceptance_criteria.given: any failing request (unknown customer, validation, auth)
acceptance_criteria.then: the body is {error:{code,message,details}} with the matching HTTP status (404 for unknown customers)

assumptions.description: Customer records already exist; customer creation is out of scope.
Bearer tokens are issued by the existing identity provider; this service only validates them.
The update is a full replacement of contact details (no PATCH / partial update).
An in-memory repository is acceptable for the prototype; production will use PostgreSQL.

technical_questions: Should email changes trigger a verification flow before taking effect?
Is rate limiting required on authentication failures?
What is the retention period for audit records?

ambiguities.description: The request does not list which contact fields are mandatory.
ambiguities.clarification_question: Which of email, phone, address line 2 are mandatory?
ambiguities.proposed_default: email, phone, line1, city, postal_code, country mandatory; line2 optional.

ambiguities.description: It is unclear whether support agents or admins may update on a customer's behalf.
ambiguities.clarification_question: Are there privileged roles that may modify any customer's contact data?
ambiguities.proposed_default: Owner-only; a privileged role can be added later.

ambiguities.description: Email uniqueness across customers is not specified.
ambiguities.clarification_question: Must an email be unique per customer?

ambiguities.description: Who may read the audit trail is not specified.
ambiguities.clarification_question: Is the audit history visible to the customer, compliance only, or both?
ambiguities.proposed_default: Owner can read their own history.

technical_design.overview: Layered FastAPI service: a thin API layer delegates to a ContactService that enforces ownership authorization, validates through Pydantic schemas, persists via a repository abstraction and records before/after state through an AuditService. Errors are raised as ApiError and rendered by central exception handlers into a uniform envelope.

components.name: Customer API
components.responsibility: HTTP routing, request parsing, response models (FastAPI)

components.name: Authentication
components.responsibility: Validate bearer tokens (HMAC-SHA256) and resolve the caller identity

components.name: Profile Service
components.responsibility: Business logic: ownership authorization, update orchestration, PII-safe logging

components.name: Validation Schemas
components.responsibility: Mandatory-field and format validation for the request payload

components.name: Repository
components.responsibility: Data-access layer for customer records (in-memory for the prototype)

components.name: Audit Service
components.responsibility: Append-only record of every contact change with before/after state

components.name: Error Handling
components.responsibility: Map ApiError / validation errors to the standard error envelope

components.name: Configuration & Logging
components.responsibility: Environment-driven settings and masked structured logging

api.description: Read the customer's current contact information.
List audit entries for the customer's contact changes (owner only).

validation_rules: email: mandatory, matches a basic RFC-5322 pattern, normalised to lower case
phone: mandatory, optional leading +, 7-15 digits after removing spaces
address.line1/city/postal_code/country: mandatory with length limits; country upper-cased ISO alpha-2
Unknown fields are ignored; the payload is a full replacement
technical_design.error_handling: Domain errors raise ApiError(status, code, message, details); a global handler renders {error:{code,message,details}}. Pydantic validation errors are converted to 422 VALIDATION_ERROR with one detail per field.
technical_design.logging: Structured log line per update with masked email/phone and the request id; authorization denials logged at WARNING. No raw PII in logs.
security: Bearer token validated with HMAC-SHA256 and constant-time comparison
Ownership check in the service layer (actor_id == customer_id) before any read or write
Signing key loaded from environment configuration, never from source
Audit log is append-only; no API deletes or edits entries

review_report.summary: Logic is correct and error handling is consistent; findings concern maintainability (duplicate authorization/lookup), testability of module singletons and unbounded audit listing. No blocking defects.

findings.finding: Authorization and lookup are repeated in get_contact and update_contact; a shared _load_owned_customer helper would remove the duplicate 404 handling.
findings.evidence: app/service.py: both methods call _authorize() then customers.get() inside try/except CustomerNotFound.
findings.recommended_fix: Extract a private helper that authorizes and loads the record, used by both methods.

findings.finding: Module-level singletons (customers, audits) make the data layer hard to swap in tests and for a future PostgreSQL implementation.
findings.evidence: app/repository.py: `customers = CustomerRepository()` / `audits = AuditRepository()` imported directly by main.py.
findings.recommended_fix: Provide the repositories through FastAPI dependencies or an app-state container.

findings.finding: The GET audit endpoint returns the full list; for long-lived customers this grows unbounded (potential performance concern).
findings.evidence: app/main.py audit_history returns every entry from service.audit_history().

security_report.summary: Authentication uses HMAC-SHA256 with constant-time comparison and ownership is enforced before every read/write; input validation is strict; no SQL/command injection or unsafe deserialization surfaces. No blocking findings; residual items are hardening recommendations.

findings.finding: No rate limiting or lockout on repeated invalid-token attempts; signature guessing is impractical with HMAC-SHA256 but the endpoint can be abused for enumeration of customer ids via 403 vs 404 responses.
findings.evidence: app/auth.py verify_token raises 401 immediately; app/service.py returns 403 before 404 so an attacker with a valid token cannot enumerate ids, but unauthenticated callers receive distinct 401/422 behaviour.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a rate limiter (e.g. per token / per IP) at the gateway and keep the 403-before-404 ordering.

findings.finding: Audit entries store full before/after contact details (PII); retention and access controls for the audit store must be defined.
findings.evidence: app/audit.py _contact_view stores email, phone and address verbatim.
findings.recommended_fix: Apply the organisation's PII retention policy to the audit store and restrict read access.

remediation_proposal.failure_summary: Security gate failed: a hard-coded signing secret was detected in app/config.py by the secret scanner, Bandit (B105) and the Security Review agent.
remediation_proposal.probable_cause: The configuration module defines JWT_SECRET as a string literal instead of reading it from the deployment environment.
remediation_proposal.rationale: Read JWT_SECRET lazily from the environment through a Settings property so the module stays importable for builds and tests while the literal secret is removed; also drops the unused `sys` import flagged by static analysis.

release_assessment.rationale: All mandatory gates passed, tests are green and no blocking findings remain. Medium-severity hardening items (rate limiting, duplicate authorization logic) should be tracked before go-live.

findings.recommended_fix: Load the key from the JWT_SECRET environment variable (or a secrets manager) and fail fast when it is missing.

--- a/app/config.py
+++ b/app/config.py
@@ -1,17 +1,28 @@
 """Application configuration.
+
+Secrets are never stored in source: the token signing key is injected through the
+``JWT_SECRET`` environment variable and read lazily so the module can be imported
+(for builds, docs generation, tests) before the deployment environment is wired up.
 
 Implements: NFR-01 (security configuration), NFR-04 (logging configuration)
 """
 
 import os
-import sys
 
 SERVICE_NAME = "customer-contact-api"
 LOG_LEVEL = "INFO"
 TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 3600
 
-# Signing key used to validate bearer tokens.
-JWT_SECRET = "hardcoded-dev-secret-9f8e7d6c5b4a3210"
+
+class MissingConfiguration(RuntimeError):
+    pass
+
+
+def _require_env(name: str) -> str:
+    value = os.environ.get(name, "").strip()
+    if not value:
+        raise MissingConfiguration(f"Required environment variable {name} is not set")
+    return value
 
 
 class Settings:
@@ -20,7 +31,7 @@
 
     @property
     def jwt_secret(self) -> str:
-        return JWT_SECRET
+        return _require_env("JWT_SECRET")
 
     @property
     def environment(self) -> str:
